name: mcp-memory-graph

tools.name: memory_store
tools.description: Store a new memory with content, metadata, and automatic vector embedding. Use this to save information, decisions, patterns, or knowledge for later semantic retrieval.

content.description: The text content to store as a memory

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

source.description: Origin of the content (e.g., file path, URL, system name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

agent_id.description: Identifier of the writing agent for multi-agent attribution

expires_at.description: Full ISO-8601 expiration timestamp, e.g. 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z (memory auto-excluded from search after this)

importance_score.description: Explicit importance 0-1 (governance/criticality). When omitted it is derived from content; min_importance filters operate on this value.

on_conflict.description: Write policy when a near-match exists. "add" (default): insert as new, except an exact duplicate is skipped (NOOP) — identical to prior behaviour. "update": merge content into the existing match (append + re-embed + version bump). "supersede": retire (invalidate) the conflicting match and add this as the current one.

volatility.description: Override the auto-derived volatility class. Omit to auto-classify from content + document_type (volatile deploy/status facts warn sooner on recall).

verification_tier.description: How well this fact is verified: source_verified > tool_verified > asserted > unverified. Lowers groundedness for unverified claims. Omit ⇒ neutral.

verification_detail.description: Free text: how/when/by-what the fact was verified (e.g. "checked live UAT DB 2026-06-18").

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search memories using hybrid vector+keyword search. Finds semantically similar content and exact keyword matches, with optional filters for scope, department, tags, date range, and temporal decay.

query.description: Search query — supports natural language for semantic search and keywords for exact matching

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

tags.description: Filter to memories containing ALL specified tags

offset.description: Skip this many results for pagination

search_mode.description: Search mode: hybrid (vector+keyword), vector only, or keyword only

type.description: Decay function type (forgetting = Ebbinghaus spaced-repetition curve)

half_life_days.description: Half-life in days for exponential decay (must be > 0)

max_age_days.description: Maximum age in days for linear decay (must be > 0)

temporal_decay.description: Apply time-based decay to favor recent memories

auto_decay.description: When true and no explicit temporal_decay is given, derive decay per result from its volatility class (volatile facts decay fast, stable facts not at all). Down-ranks stale volatile facts without hand-tuning a half-life.

date_from.description: Filter: only memories created at/after this full ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z)

date_to.description: Filter: only memories created at/before this full ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-03-31T23:59:59Z)

min_groundedness.description: Minimum TRUST threshold (0-1), distinct from min_confidence (relevance). Drops results whose groundedness — stored confidence_score + provenance tier + recency — is below this. Use to demand well-sourced memories.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 point-in-time: return memories that were valid at this instant (bi-temporal). Defaults to currently-valid memories when omitted. Must be a full ISO-8601 timestamp (date + time + zone); a date-only or non-padded value is rejected to avoid a silently-wrong lexicographic slice.

use_graph.description: Enable HippoRAG multi-hop recall: seed the entity graph from the query and fuse Personalized PageRank as a third ranker, surfacing memories connected through entities (associative recall) that pure vector+keyword search misses. Default false.

rerank.description: Enable local cross-encoder reranking: reorder the top candidates by joint (query, document) relevance using a cross-encoder model — the biggest precision win over the bi-encoder base embedder. Slower (runs a model per candidate) and lazy-loads the model on first use. Defaults ON at the MCP server (precision matters more than latency for agent recall); pass false to skip. Left unset, programmatic callers do not rerank.

rerank_top_n.description: How many top candidates to rerank when "rerank" is true (default 50). Higher = better recall coverage but slower.

detail_level.description: Controls response detail: "summary" returns titles + snippets (default, saves tokens), "full" returns complete content, "ids_only" returns just IDs and titles for browsing

max_tokens.description: Approximate maximum response size in tokens (~4 chars per token). Results are truncated to fit within budget. Applies after detail_level projection.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Retrieve a specific memory by its ID. Optionally include child chunks for ingested documents.

include_chunks.description: If true, also return child chunks for ingested documents

tools.name: memory_update
tools.description: Update an existing memory. If content changes, the vector embedding is automatically regenerated. Previous versions are preserved in history.

id.description: ID of the memory to update

expires_at.description: New full ISO-8601 expiration timestamp (e.g. 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z), or null to remove

changed_by.description: Who made this change (for version history)

verification_tier.description: Set/upgrade the verification tier after the fact (the main post-hoc use case — you verify a stored claim against live state later). Raises/lowers groundedness.

verification_detail.description: Free text accompanying a verification_tier change.

volatility.description: Manual override of the auto-derived volatility class.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete memories by ID or by filter criteria (scope, department, before_date, expired_only). Provide at least one of id or filter.

id.description: Delete a specific memory by ID

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

before_date.description: Delete memories created before this full ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC, e.g. 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z)

expired_only.description: If true, only delete expired memories

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: Browse memories with filtering and pagination. Supports sorting by creation date, update date, or title.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

offset.description: Skip this many results for pagination

as_of.description: ISO 8601 point-in-time: return memories that were valid at this instant (bi-temporal). Defaults to currently-valid memories when omitted. Must be a full ISO-8601 timestamp (date + time + zone); a date-only or non-padded value is rejected to avoid a silently-wrong lexicographic slice.

tools.name: memory_ingest
tools.description: Ingest a full document: automatically chunks it based on content type (text, markdown, code, legal), embeds each chunk, and stores with provenance. Use this for large documents.

source.description: Origin of the content (e.g., file path, URL, system name)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

chunk_size.description: Target chunk size in characters (~4 chars per token)

chunk_overlap.description: Overlap between chunks in characters for context preservation

tools.name: memory_related
tools.description: Find memories semantically related to a given memory ID. Uses vector similarity to discover connections.

id.description: Memory ID to find related memories for

limit.description: Maximum number of related memories to return

tools.name: memory_versions
tools.description: View the version history of a memory, showing all past edits with timestamps and who made each change.

id.description: Memory ID to get version history for

limit.description: Maximum number of versions to return

tools.name: memory_stats
tools.description: Get usage statistics: total memories, chunks, documents, breakdowns by scope/department/type, storage size, and expired count.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

tools.name: memory_verify
tools.description: Verify the signed provenance envelope of memories: recomputes each content_hash and ed25519-checks the signature against THIS machine's trusted signing key (not the row's self-embedded key). Verify one by id, or a batch by scope/namespace. Returns per-memory status (verified / unsigned / tampered / untrusted) + a summary {verified, unsigned, tampered, untrusted}. "untrusted" = validly signed but by a non-trust-root key (e.g. a teammate on a synced vault) — distinct from "tampered". Read-only. Signing is enabled by MCP_SIGN_MEMORIES.

id.description: Verify a single memory by id. Omit to verify a batch by scope/namespace.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

limit.description: Max memories to verify in batch mode (default 100)

trusted_pubkeys.description: Additional trusted signer public keys (SPKI PEM) for multi-machine/team vaults — a memory signed by any of these (or by MCP_TRUSTED_PUBKEYS, or this machine's own key) verifies instead of reading 'untrusted'.

tools.name: memory_tiers
tools.description: Show the MemGPT-style tier distribution (hot / recall / archival) of currently-valid, top-level memories and list the hot working set. Tiers are derived from access recency + frequency — hot = frequently or recently accessed, archival = old and rarely touched, recall = everything in between. Read-only; optional scope/namespace filter.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: memory_export
tools.description: Export memories as JSON for backup or migration. Supports filtering by scope, namespace, and department. Max 1000 records per export.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

limit.description: Maximum memories to export in this page (live, top-level only)

offset.description: Pagination offset; use with has_more to export a large corpus in pages

tools.name: memory_import
tools.description: Import memories from JSON. Each item is embedded and stored. Use overwrite=true to update existing memories by ID.

content.description: The text content of the memory

id.description: Optional ID — if omitted, a new ID is generated

anyOf.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

anyOf.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

anyOf.description: Origin of the content (e.g., file path, URL, system name)

source.description: Origin of the content (e.g., file path, URL, system name)

anyOf.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

agent_id.description: Originating actor/agent id (preserved on restore for attribution)

created_at.description: Original creation timestamp (ISO 8601) — preserved on restore

updated_at.description: Original update timestamp (ISO 8601) — preserved on restore

importance_score.description: Explicit importance 0-1 — preserved on restore (falls back to the content-derived heuristic only when absent), so a backup keeps criticality

confidence_score.description: Explicit confidence/trust 0-1 — preserved on restore so a backup keeps groundedness

data.description: Array of memory objects to import (max 500 per batch)

overwrite.description: If true, overwrite existing memories with same ID

tools.name: vault_sync
tools.description: Sync an Obsidian vault to memory. Scans for markdown files, extracts frontmatter/tags/wiki-links, embeds content, and stores as searchable memories. Uses incremental sync based on file modification times.

vault_path.description: Absolute path to the Obsidian vault directory

chunk_size.description: Target chunk size in characters for large files (~4 chars per token)

chunk_overlap.description: Overlap between chunks in characters for context preservation

force.description: If true, re-sync all files regardless of modification time

include_patterns.description: Only sync files matching these glob patterns (e.g., ["notes/**", "projects/**"])

exclude_patterns.description: Skip files matching these glob patterns (e.g., ["templates/**", "daily/**"])

tools.name: vault_status
tools.description: Check the sync status of an Obsidian vault: total files, synced/pending/changed counts, last sync time, and memory count.

vault_path.description: Absolute path to the Obsidian vault directory

tools.name: vault_search
tools.description: Search memories via hybrid vector+keyword search, scoped to a namespace. Defaults the namespace to the vault folder name; pass an explicit `namespace` to search memories that live under a different namespace (e.g. after memory_export_vault).

vault_path.description: Absolute path to the Obsidian vault directory

query.description: Search query — supports natural language for semantic search and keywords for exact matching

namespace.description: Namespace to search. Defaults to the vault folder name — set this when your memories live in a namespace different from the vault directory name (e.g. after memory_export_vault wrote them under <vault>/<namespace>/).

offset.description: Skip this many results for pagination

search_mode.description: Search mode: hybrid (vector+keyword), vector only, or keyword only

tags.description: Filter to memories containing ALL specified tags

tools.name: memory_export_vault
tools.description: Write memories OUT to an Obsidian vault as .md files with YAML frontmatter — the reverse of vault_sync. Each currently-valid top-level memory becomes a plain markdown file a human can open and edit; namespaced memories land under <vault>/<namespace>/. Lossless: written files parse back via the vault parser. Optionally filter by scope/namespace.

vault_path.description: Absolute path to the target Obsidian vault directory (created if missing). Memories are written as .md files with YAML frontmatter — the reverse of vault_sync.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: memory_canvas
tools.description: Export the memory graph as a JSON Canvas 1.0 .canvas — opens as a spatial board in real Obsidian. Each currently-valid top-level memory becomes a text node on a deterministic grid; memory_links become labeled, arrow-tipped edges. Optionally filter by scope/namespace and cap with limit. When vault_path is given the canvas is written there (confined under the vault) and its path returned; otherwise only the canvas object.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

limit.description: Maximum memories to include as canvas nodes (default 50)

vault_path.description: Absolute path to an Obsidian vault directory (created if missing). When given, the canvas is written there as a .canvas file (confined under the vault) and its path is returned; otherwise only the canvas object is returned.

name.description: Filename stem for the written .canvas (default "memory-graph"). Sanitized — path separators and ".." can never escape the vault.

tools.name: memory_consolidate
tools.description: Run the "dream cycle": find and merge near-duplicate memories, prune expired/low-quality entries, and update quality scores based on access patterns. Use dry_run=true to preview changes.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

similarity_threshold.description: Cosine similarity threshold for duplicate detection (0.5-1.0)

prune_expired.description: Remove memories past their expires_at date

prune_low_quality.description: Remove memories with both low importance and low confidence

dry_run.description: If true, report what would be done without making changes

max_operations.description: Maximum number of merge/prune operations per run

forgetting_floor.description: Opt-in spaced-repetition prune. When set (0-1), remove weakly-held memories whose retention e^(-Δt/stability) has decayed below this floor. Omit to disable.

tools.name: memory_extract_learnings
tools.description: Extract decisions, patterns, error fixes, and conventions from a session transcript using heuristic analysis. Deduplicates against existing memories and optionally auto-stores.

transcript.description: Session transcript or conversation text to extract learnings from

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

categories.description: Which categories of learnings to extract (default: all)

auto_store.description: If true, automatically store extracted learnings as memories

tools.name: memory_manifest
tools.description: Get a lightweight index of all memories — titles, types, tags, and scores without content. Use this to discover what knowledge exists before running expensive searches.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

document_type.description: Type of document (e.g., contract, policy, code, incident, decision)

offset.description: Skip this many entries for pagination

tools.name: memory_graph
tools.description: Query the knowledge graph: find entities, their relationships, and linked memories. Use entity name to start traversal, or browse all entities by type. Supports multi-hop traversal (depth 1-3).

entity.description: Entity name to start graph traversal from

include_memories.description: Include linked memories in the response

tools.name: memory_extract_entities
tools.description: Store LLM-extracted entities and relationships for a memory. The calling agent should analyze memory content and provide structured entity/relationship data. This enables knowledge graph queries.

memory_id.description: Memory ID to associate extracted entities with

entities.description: Entities extracted from the memory content

tools.name: memory_condense
tools.description: Apply agent-generated summaries to condense old memories. Preserves original content for later restoration. Use after consolidation reports flag condensation candidates.

memories.description: Batch of memories with agent-generated summaries

tools.name: memory_restore
tools.description: Bring a memory back: un-tombstones a soft-forgotten memory (memory_forget {hard:false}) by clearing valid_to/tx_expired so it re-enters default recall, AND/OR restores a condensed memory to its original full content. Both are applied when both apply. Returns reinstated/uncondensed flags.

id.description: Memory ID to bring back — un-tombstones a soft-forgotten memory and/or restores condensed content to original full text

tools.name: memory_query
tools.description: Answer a question with a TIGHT, relevant subgraph instead of flooding context. Seeds from hybrid search, walks the memory graph (hub-avoiding) up to max_hops, and returns a token-budgeted "context" string plus structured nodes — with an actionable hint when truncated.

query.description: The question to answer. Seeds from hybrid search, then walks the memory graph to return a tight, relevant subgraph instead of flooding context.

max_tokens.description: Approximate token budget for the rendered context (~4 chars per token). Nodes are rendered until the budget is hit, then truncated with a hint.

max_hops.description: How many hops to walk out from the seed memories (1-4).

seed_limit.description: Maximum seed memories from the initial search. A gap cutoff drops seeds scoring below 20% of the top seed to keep the traversal focused.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: core_memory_get
tools.description: Read the pinned "core memory" block for a (scope, namespace) — a small, bounded, always-in-context note the agent maintains about who it is and what matters now. Returns content, char_limit, and used (character count).

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: core_memory_append
tools.description: Append text to the pinned core-memory block (newline-separated when non-empty). If the result would exceed char_limit the write is refused (error: core_memory_full) so you compact via core_memory_replace instead of silently overflowing.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

text.description: Text to append to the pinned core-memory block (newline-separated when the block is non-empty). Refused if it would exceed char_limit — compact via core_memory_replace instead.

tools.name: core_memory_replace
tools.description: Replace the first occurrence of old_text with new_text in the pinned core-memory block. Returns error: not_found if old_text is absent, or core_memory_full if the result would exceed char_limit. Use this to update or compact the block.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

old_text.description: Substring to find (first occurrence) in the core-memory block

new_text.description: Replacement text for the first occurrence of old_text

tools.name: memory_reflect
tools.description: Generative-Agents-style reflection (agent-driven, no LLM in the server). mode:"gather" (default) returns the most reflection-worthy memories (high importance × recent) as material plus an instruction to synthesize 1–3 higher-level insights. mode:"store" persists a synthesized insight (provenance="reflection") and "derived_from"-links it to its source memories.

mode.description: "gather" (default): the server SELECTs the most reflection-worthy memories (high importance × recent) as material for you to synthesize. "store": persist a synthesized insight back, linked to its source memories.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

limit.description: gather: max reflection-material rows to return (default 10)

insight.description: store: the higher-level insight you synthesized from the gathered material

title.description: store: optional short title for the stored insight

source_ids.description: store: ids of the source memories this insight was derived from (linked via "derived_from"; non-existent ids are skipped)

tools.name: memory_communities
tools.description: GraphRAG global sensemaking (agent-driven, no LLM in the server). Detects communities (densely-connected entity clusters) over the entity graph on demand via weighted label propagation, and returns each community's top entities + linked memories. This is the corpus-level view that chunk-level search can't give — synthesize named themes from the communities to answer "what are the main themes?".

limit.description: Maximum communities to return, largest first (default 20)

min_size.description: Drop communities with fewer than this many entities (default 1)

tools.name: memory_template
tools.description: Fetch an Obsidian-style note scaffold for a document_type so stored memories stay structurally consistent. Returns a markdown template with ## Section headers (e.g., decision → Context/Decision/Consequences; incident → Symptom/Root Cause/Fix/Prevention; also learning, bug-fix, meeting, session). Unknown types get a generic Summary/Details/Notes scaffold (known:false). Read-only: fill the scaffold, then store it via memory_store.

document_type.description: Document type to fetch a note scaffold for (e.g., decision, incident, learning, bug-fix, meeting, session). Unknown types get a generic Summary/Details/Notes scaffold (known:false).

tools.name: memory_session_note
tools.description: Frictionless per-session capture ("daily note for agents"). Keyed by source "session:<session_id>": the first call creates one session memory (document_type "session"); every later call for the same session_id appends to that same memory (newline-joined, re-embedded and versioned). Different session_ids stay isolated. Returns { memory_id, created, appended }.

session_id.description: Session identifier. The note is keyed by source "session:<session_id>" — the first call creates the memory, later calls append to that same one.

text.description: Text to capture (created as content, or appended newline-joined to the session note).

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

title.description: Optional title used only on create (defaults to "Session <session_id>").

tools.name: memory_attribution
tools.description: Multi-agent / team attribution rollup. Returns how many currently-valid top-level memories each agent (agent_id, set at store time) wrote — { by_agent, by_author, total } — distinct from author (the human/source). Memories stored without an agent_id are bucketed under "unattributed". Optional scope/namespace filters scope the rollup.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: memory_questions
tools.description: Active "questions to ask" digest. Surfaces open questions / gaps the graph is uniquely positioned to find so you know what to verify or learn next: AMBIGUOUS inferred links to confirm (verify), frequently-mentioned but barely-documented entities (gap), and disconnected memories that may be stale or mis-scoped (orphan). Returns { questions: [{ question, type, evidence }], count } over currently-valid top-level memories. Optional scope/namespace filters and limit (default 20).

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

limit.description: Maximum number of questions to return (default 20)

tools.name: memory_forget
tools.description: GDPR-grade forget (additive — does NOT replace memory_delete). hard:false (default) soft-deletes/tombstones: stamps valid_to so the memory is excluded from default retrieval but stays queryable via as_of and is recoverable. hard:true erases for real: returns a portability "export" copy FIRST (data-subject access), THEN permanently deletes (irreversible, cascades). Returns { forgotten, mode, recoverable, export? }.

hard.description: Erasure mode. false (default): soft-delete/tombstone — stamps valid_to so the memory is excluded from default retrieval but remains queryable via as_of and is recoverable. true: hard erase — returns a portability export copy FIRST (data-subject access), THEN permanently deletes (irreversible, cascades). Additive — the existing memory_delete tool is unaffected.

tools.name: memory_history
tools.description: Point-in-time history surface for one memory: its current bi-temporal timeline (created_at/updated_at/valid_from/valid_to/tx_expired/superseded_at/version) plus the full memory_versions edit history. Returns { memory_id, exists, timeline, versions } or { memory_id, exists:false }.

id.description: Memory ID to get the bi-temporal timeline + version history for

tools.name: memory_unlinked_mentions
tools.description: Surface "unlinked mentions" for a memory — other memories that are semantically related (vector-near + shared entities) but that you have NOT explicitly linked yet. This is Obsidian's killer feature, automated: instead of matching note titles as literal text, it uses embeddings + the entity graph to propose latent connections the agent never made. Auto "similar_to" suggestions are surfaced; existing wikilink/co-occurrence/typed links are excluded. Use it to discover and then confirm real connections (e.g. via memory_extract_entities or a stored link).

id.description: Memory ID to surface unlinked mentions for

limit.description: Maximum number of unlinked mentions to return

min_similarity.description: Minimum cosine similarity for a mention (0-1)

tools.name: memory_link_check
tools.description: Find BROKEN [[wikilinks]] — the inverse of memory_unlinked_mentions. Reports (1) unresolved: a [[Title]] in a memory's content that matches no LIVE memory title in the same scope/namespace; (2) dangling_edges: stored wikilink edges whose target memory was deleted or superseded. Resolution is by TITLE (memories have no slug) so write [[Exact Title]]. Pass an id to check one memory, or scope/namespace to sweep a partition. Read-only.

id.description: Check one memory by ID. Omit to sweep a whole partition (scope/namespace).

scope.description: Sweep scope (when no id is given)

namespace.description: Sweep namespace (when no id is given)

limit.description: Max source memories to inspect in a sweep

tools.name: memory_query_structured
tools.description: Structured query over memory PROPERTIES (the agent's "Bases/Dataview"): filter currently-valid, top-level memories by scope/namespace/department/document_type/language/tags (AND)/min_importance/created_at range, sort by created_at|updated_at|importance_score|title, paginate, and project specific fields. Exact, deterministic retrieval that complements fuzzy memory_search — use it for "all decision memories in namespace=acme with importance>0.7, newest first".

tags.description: All listed tags must be present (AND)

tools.name: memory_version_diff
tools.description: Show a line-by-line diff between two revisions of a memory (Obsidian-Sync-grade trust). `to` defaults to the current version. Use it to audit exactly what an edit changed — added/removed lines plus a summary count.

to.description: Version to diff to (defaults to current)

tools.name: memory_version_restore
tools.description: Roll a memory back to a prior version's content. The restore is itself a versioned, re-embedded edit (the pre-restore state is snapshotted, the vault file re-mirrored) — never a destructive overwrite. Returns the restored memory.

version.description: Version number to restore content from

tools.name: memory_webhook
tools.description: Manage the active-infrastructure event bus (gated on MCP_WEBHOOKS). register an outbound webhook target (URL is SSRF-validated — public http(s) only), list targets (secrets never returned), delete a target, or dispatch the durable delivery queue now. Mutations to memories (created/updated/superseded/deleted/forgotten) enqueue HMAC-signed deliveries that this tool drains with retry + circuit-breaker + dead-letter.

action.description: register a target | list targets | delete a target | dispatch the queue now

url.description: Target URL (action=register). Validated against the SSRF guard: public http(s) only.

secret.description: Optional HMAC-SHA256 signing secret; sent as X-Memory-Signature on each delivery.

scope.description: Only deliver events for memories in this scope.

namespace.description: Only deliver events for memories in this namespace.

tools.name: memory_insights
tools.description: Active advisor digest: what in the store needs ATTENTION now — unresolved conflicts, memories flagged stale by change-propagation, most-contradicted facts, and decisions recorded with no supporting evidence. Complements memory_questions (what to capture next). Read-only; optionally scoped.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

limit.description: Maximum number of insights to return (default 20)

tools.name: memory_health
tools.description: Store health report: live/retired/stale counts, aging buckets, unresolved conflicts, and webhook delivery health, rolled up to a single ok|attention status with reasons. Read-only; optionally scoped.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: memory_revalidate
tools.description: Change-propagation surface. action=list: memories flagged needs_revalidation (a source they were derived from changed). action=preview: the blast radius of a change to `id` (which dependents WOULD be flagged) without mutating anything. action=confirm: clear `id`'s stale flag after re-verifying it.

action.description: list stale memories | preview the blast radius of a change to `id` (dry-run) | confirm `id` is current

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: memory_session_state
tools.description: Save or resume a resumable session-state ("where was I"): structured summary/next_steps/open_questions/files_touched/branch keyed by session_key. save upserts (versioned, so you can diff sessions via memory_version_diff); resume returns the latest. Bypasses the dedup write-gate so an incremental save always persists.

action.description: save the current session state | resume the latest

session_key.description: Stable key for the work thread (defaults to branch, else "default").

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

next_steps.description: Ordered list of what to do next.

branch.description: Git branch this session is on.

tools.name: memory_expertise
tools.description: Adaptive per-user expertise profile. action=observe records demonstrated knowledge of a topic (level rises on a saturating curve, never collapses other topics); action=get returns the profile. The agent supplies the classified topic — the server just tracks evidence over time.

action.description: observe demonstrated knowledge of a topic | get the profile

topic.description: The topic (required for observe; optional filter for get).

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

tools.name: memory_export_dataset
tools.description: Export high-signal rows (auto-extracted learnings + agent reflections) as instruction→output training pairs (pairs/chatml/alpaca) for a project LoRA/distillation flywheel. Read-only, quality-filtered by importance/confidence. Training stays out of the repo — this only emits the JSONL.

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

format.description: Output shape: {prompt,completion} | ChatML messages | Alpaca instruction/output.

tools.name: memory_lesson
tools.description: Capture a structured lesson or incident in one call: fills the matching section template (incident → Symptom/Root Cause/Fix/Prevention; lesson → What/Why it matters/How to apply) from your field values and stores it through the normal write path (deduped — a repeat capture is a NOOP). Unknown document_types use a generic scaffold.

document_type.description: Section template to fill: lesson | incident | decision | bug-fix | meeting | session. Unknown types use a generic Summary/Details/Notes scaffold.

fields.description: Section values keyed by section name (snake_case ok), e.g. {symptom, root_cause, fix, prevention} for an incident or {what, why_it_matters, how_to_apply} for a lesson. Omitted sections keep a placeholder.

title.description: Optional title (auto-derived from the first field value when omitted)

namespace.description: Namespace within scope (e.g., project name, team name)

department.description: Department (e.g., legal, engineering, hr, sales, finance)

source.description: Origin of the content (e.g., file path, URL, system name)

importance_score.description: Manual importance 0–1 (higher surfaces first in reflection/recall)

instructions: Local-first, bi-temporal knowledge-memory server. Persist and recall durable knowledge (facts, decisions, patterns, fixes) across sessions; everything runs on this machine ($0/token, no cloud). WRITE: memory_store for one discrete fact/decision/pattern (always pass a title); memory_ingest for a large document (auto-chunks); memory_session_note for a running session log; core_memory_append for always-on pinned context. READ: memory_search to recall by meaning (rerank defaults ON); add use_graph:true for multi-hop. memory_query for a token-budgeted context block answering a question; memory_query_structured for exact metadata filters; memory_manifest to discover what exists. Scopes are global|project|user|team|department. An unscoped memory_search HIDES scope="user" memories — if a personal memory seems missing, re-search with scope:"user". Prefer memory_forget (recoverable tombstone, GDPR-aware) over memory_delete (hard, irreversible). Run memory_consolidate with dry_run:true before a real consolidation.
